items.title: RealPRO Select helps lift Realtor.com revenue
items.description: Move , the parent company of Realtor.com , said the momentum generated by RealPRO Select in fiscal year 2026 has carried over into the first quarter of fiscal year 2027. During the first quarter of FY 2027, Realtor.com recorded $160 million in revenue, up 5% year over year, marking the segment’s eighth consecutive quarter of growth. These financial results were highlighted during News Corp ’s fiscal year 2026 fourth-quarter earnings call on Wednesday evening. “In a housing market constrained by 7%-plus mortgage rates , Damian [Eales] and the team have exhibited exceptional discipline in their operational focus and AI integration, and that approach has converted revenue growth into meaningful bottom-line expansion,” Robert Thomson, the CEO of News Corp, said during the earnings call. RealPRO Select grows News Corp executives attributed Realtor.com ’s strong revenue performance to the growth of RealPRO Select. The company said it is focused on enhancing the platform with stronger lead generation, branding, productivity tools and training capabilities. Realtor.com also focused on the expansion of RealAssist AI during Q1, including the launch of a pilot of RealAssist in Rich Communication Services (RCS), integrated directly into Google search and available on iOS and Android. “The pilot is already attracting new users, driving strong engagement, and helping us capture pre-search intent earlier in the buyer journey before consumers ever enter a browser,” Damian Eales, the CEO of Move, wrote in a blog post about the company's quarterly performance. In addition, Realtor.com also launched RealAssist AI for Realtor.com+, which Eales said helps agents onboard their clients faster, build more tailored searches, summarize client activity and draft follow-ups in their own voice. “The platform is already supporting thousands of successful agent-client connections, and early feedback on these AI tools has been very positive,” Eales wrote. Other highlights Eales also highlighted the relaunch of the My Home dashboard, which now includes a collaboration with Opendoor . Eales said this is encouraging sellers to engage a listing agent much earlier in their journey. In addition, News Corp also noted that Comscore data shows 4.9 visits per unique user to Realtor.com, up 8% annually, and an average of 263 million monthly visits in the quarter, which the company said represents a “substantial” lead over Redfin and Homes.com . Despite these strong numbers, Realtor.com noted that lead volume was down 11%, which the portal attributed to broader market conditions and its repositioning of customer acquisitions to higher-quality and higher-value leads. “Despite a constrained housing market , Realtor.com’s strategy is delivering positive results, and we’re well positioned to grow as conditions improve,” Eales wrote. “Our focus remains on investing in our audience and AI tools that enhance a consumer’s experience and augment the role of the professional agent.” Overall, News Corp’s digital real estate services segment generated $529 million in revenue, up 10% from a year prior. The company as a whole generated $2.28 billion in revenue, a 6% annual increase, and net income of $215 million, up 43% compared to a year prior. Related More: Earnings News Corp. Realtor.com

items.title: American Housing Corp names leadership for new Austin division
items.description: The American Housing Corporation launched an Austin homebuilding division and named three industry veterans to lead the new operation as it ramps up an infill-focused, prefabricated rowhome platform, the company announced this week. Austin is the launch market for the company’s infill homebuilding strategy, which centers on designing, manufacturing and constructing urban rowhomes. The move comes as builders look for ways to add “missing middle” housing in supply-constrained, high-cost markets without relying solely on traditional greenfield development. Parker Scott, a former division president at LGI Homes , was appointed general manager, Daniel Green will serve as director of construction operations and Luke Allen will serve as director of land. Scott brings more than 20 years of homebuilding sales and operational experience to the role. Green joins from senior construction positions at Homebound , ATCO Structures and Perry Homes , where he focused on building operations and execution systems. Allen, who previously held land roles at Lennar and Ashton Woods , will oversee land acquisition, underwriting and pipeline development for the Austin market. In October 2026, American Housing Corp completed its “Demo 2” prototype using a componentized, prefabricated building system. The company is building a 250,000-square-foot manufacturing plant in Southeast Austin designed to produce up to 1,200 homes annually, according to the announcement. The factory-scale approach is intended to standardize production, shorten build times and provide more cost certainty, which could appeal to capital providers and municipalities looking for scalable infill housing solutions. For real estate investors and lenders, the combination of an infill land strategy with a controlled-offsite construction environment could change underwriting assumptions around cycle times and construction risk. Alongside the Austin division launch, the company restructured its real estate operations and parted ways with co-founder Bobby Fijan. The firm credited Fijan with helping establish its early real estate footprint and championing urban, family-sized housing. Related More: homebuilder Texas

items.title: Onity's 50%+ recapture rate raises the bar for servicers
items.description: Onity's 50%+ recapture rate raises the bar for servicers By Colin McNamara Published November 05, 2026, 4:24 p.m. EST 2 Min Read Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Email What's at Stake: Whether smaller lenders can maintain volume as the market enters a difficult 2027. Supporting Data: After spending last quarter in the red, Onity recorded $3.5 million in net income attributable to common shareholders and $29.6 million in adjusted pretax income. Overview bullets generated by AI with editorial review. Onity Group's recapture rate topped 50% in the third quarter, up 18 percentage points from a year ago. The lender is using its servicing book to grow volume while the rest of the industry shrinks. The servicing segment produced $7 million in pretax income and $29 million on an adjusted basis, up from $12 million in the second quarter. Originations totaled $23.7 million in adjusted pretax income, down 15% from $27.8 million the previous quarter, according to the company's third quarter earnings release. Processing Content "The big benefit for them is being a relatively large servicer," Bose George, mortgage finance analyst at Keefe, Bruyette & Woods, told National Mortgage News. "In the higher-for-longer rate environment , they are somewhat better positioned being a big servicer with a smaller origination footprint." A model for smaller lenders Onity's performance signals a shift some lenders can make. While it's difficult for larger originators to outperform the market due to their scale, George said, smaller lenders should take a more servicing-forward approach to maintain volume as the market enters what is expected to be a difficult year in 2027. Glen Messina, chairman, president and CEO at Onity "In a market environment that is increasingly favorable for servicing and more challenging for originations, our complementary businesses returned the company to profitability and more than doubled adjusted return on equity from the prior quarter," Onity President and CEO Glen Messina said in a press release Thursday. Growing the servicing book Onity reported $24.7 billion in total servicing additions last quarter, bringing its total unpaid balance to $343 billion, up 9% from the same quarter last year. Subservicing additions reached $53 billion by the end of the quarter, exceeding its full-year target. Chief Financial Officer Sean O'Neil said on the earnings call that Onity plans to be more selective in its expansion going forward. Cost advantage The company has been pursuing efficiencies by reducing its headcount and improving technology. It did not disclose layoffs on the call, but said its investments have decreased the cost per loan to $94, below the independent mortgage bank average of $112 per loan. "The technology, not just for them but the whole industry, has really improved," George said. "The expectation is that costs will continue to come down as technology becomes more efficient." Earnings turnaround After spending last quarter in the red, Onity recorded $3.5 million in net income attributable to common shareholders and $29.6 million in adjusted pretax income. Both came in below last year's marks but were notable improvements over its second-quarter performance, which featured a $12.9 million net loss. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $2.93, beating BTIG's prediction of $1.60 and S&P Capital IQ's consensus estimate of $1.67. Revenue totaled $278.1 million, down slightly from $282.9 million in the second quarter and $280.3 million last year. Colin McNamara Reporter Colin McNamara is a reporter for National Mortgage News. items.title: Bobby Flay and Brooke Williamson Reveal What It’s Like To Have 2 Celebrity Chefs in a Home Kitchen—and How They’re Prepping for Thanksgiving
items.description: Food Network chefs Bobby Flay and Brooke Williamson are getting ready for another Thanksgiving celebration at their beautiful Hamptons home, and they've shared their best tips and tricks ahead of the holiday. In an interview with People magazine, the power couple said that their best advice is to start dinner prep early. “Prep as much as you can ahead of time,” said Williamson, 48. “I think stuffing tastes better the next day, once it’s had a chance to meld together.” Flay , 61, dropped another helpful piece of advice: “Have chicken stock on your stove. It reheats the sliced turkey, which ultimately gets dried out no matter what you do. It can also thin out gravy that gets too thick.” While one might assume that having two celebrity chefs in a household can feel like a case of too many cooks in the kitchen, the duo said it’s never a problem for them. Loading... Celebrity chefs Bobby Flay and Brooke Williamson are preparing to host a Tuscan-inspired Thanksgiving dinner. Winnie Au/PEOPLE Loading... The couple shared a look at the home kitchen of their New York City residence with People magazine. Winnie Au/PEOPLE Loading... Despite each having command of the kitchen, they say "it never feels like we're in each other's way." Winnie Au/PEOPLE “We definitely split up the work,” said Williamson. “It never feels like we’re in each other’s way. It feels like it makes sense.” Flay and Williamson invited the publication into the kitchen of their New York City home, showing off the gorgeous cabinets and generously sized island. After a recent trip to Italy , the couple told the magazine that they’re planning a Tuscan-inspired feast this year, joking that it’ll be a “mini ‘Brady Bunch’” scenario with their blended families. Flay is dad to 30-year-old Sophie , while Williamson has a son, Hudson , 18. In September, Flay spoke about the home kitchens he has in his two residences—his Tribeca pad and an estate in the Hamptons. “The kitchen is spacious, and I make three meals a day in there,” he told The Wall Street Journal . ”The space relaxes me and allows me to cook for family and friends.” In his home out East, the kitchen is not just a place to whip up delicious meals. The room functions more like a full-fledged restaurant. “On the other side of my sizable island are three French cafe tables for guests,” he explained. The setup is even equipped with a professional fryer, which he described as a “recent kitchen splurge.” Among his latest kitchen tools is a utensil he’s relied on for years: “I still have the chef’s knife I used at [the French Culinary Institute],” he shared. “When [I] prepare food with it, the feel reminds me that I’m still learning every day." The kitchen of the Amagansett home is his favorite place to cook and where he has typically hosted Thanksgiving. Loading... Flay recently gifted Williamson a gorgeous diamond ring to show his commitment without entering another marriage. Winnie Au/PEOPLE Flay built the dwelling from the ground up during his marriage to “Law and Order: SVU” actress Stephanie March . The former couple, who divorced in 2015, hosted a turkey dinner for a staggering 50 guests at their first Thanksgiving in the home. “I prepared two 30-pound turkeys and cooked sides for days,” he recalled in a 2013 interview with Elle Decor . “I stand at my kitchen island from the minute I get out here to the minute I leave.” Although Flay has publicly discussed his desire to steer clear of matrimony after three divorces, he and Williamson have agreed on an alternative way to show their commitment to each other. “She’s like, ‘I just want a big ring and a big party,’ and I was like, ‘I love that idea because my marriages have not lasted, unfortunately,’” he told People. Explaining that the “most important thing” is to “make sure that Brooke feels like she’s committed to,” he recalled of the moment he gifted her a “giant diamond ring” during a trip to London. Williamson describes the flashy piece of jewelry as “the perfect ring,” adding that “it’s very sparkly.” Although she was initially thrown off by the gesture, she now sports the rock on her right hand. “I thought it was incredibly thoughtful,” said Williamson. “He said just because I don’t feel the need to get married or want to get married again doesn’t mean that you don’t deserve the big, beautiful ring that comes along with it.” While Flay has been private about his past relationships, he admits he’s been more open this time around, and cites all they have in common for his “confidence” about their partnership. “I feel very confident about this,” he said of the pair’s connection. “There’s so many wonderful things about it.” Get real estate news in your inbox Sign up now Hannah Chambers is a senior celebrity and lifestyle reporter who joined Realtor.com in 2026. She has been writing entertainment and lifestyle content since 2016, with her work appearing in Cosmopolitan, BravoTV, NYLON, Bustle, Elite Daily, and The Zoe Report, among other publications. Hannah received a bachelor’s degree in journalism from The University of Maine. In her spare time, she loves to chat about pop culture and is a major fan of reality TV.

items.title: California People and Company News, Week of Nov. 6, 2026
items.description: California CRE News In Your Inbox. Sign up for Connect emails to stay informed with CRE stories that are 150 words or less. California + Finance | November 5, 2026 By: Paul Bubny California People and Company News, Week of Nov. 6, 2026 Colliers has added industrial professionals Greg Lewis, Andy Irwin and Ryan Spradling, who have joined its San Diego brokerage as EVPs Joining Colliers from JLL, the team brings more than six decades of combined experience and a longstanding track record advising industrial occupiers, institutional owners, developers and investors throughout San Diego. LTC Properties, Inc. , a REIT specializing in seniors housing and healthcare properties, appointed Eric Clark as SVP, corporate finance and investor relations, a newly created position. Clark will lead and manage LTC’s capital markets, financial forecasting and investor relations functions. He joins LTC from BTIG, where he served as managing director, investment banking focused on capital markets and mergers and acquisitions. PML LLC, a NYC-based strategic advisory and project management firm, has appointed Jeff Carlisle VP of its West Coast operations. Carlisle brings significant local, national and international experience with a proven track record in a wide variety of building sectors. For 2026, the CREDA SoCal UCLA vs. USC Real Estate Challenge Honorary Coaches will be Richard Ziman, co-founder and founding chairman of Rexford Industrial Realty , and Wilbur H. “Wil” Smith III, owner, CEO, and president of Greenlaw Partners. The student teams, which are currently tied at 14 wins apiece, will be competing for the coveted Silver Shovel. HBA Los Angeles, the flagship studio of the global hospitality design firm, has added Gianpiero Gaglione as principal. A respected designer and creative leader with more than 20 years of international experience, Gaglione joins HBA Los Angeles following more than six years of running his eponymous design practice. HomeRise’s board of directors has appointed Ancel Romero, CPM, NAHP-E, FHC, as CEO. Romero is a former HomeRise board member who has spent more than two decades leading affordable housing property management. He will lead the wind-down HomeRise announced on Oct.1. The Kleinfelder Group, Inc., a leading engineering, design, construction management, construction materials inspection and testing, and environmental professional services firm, appointed Galen Cooter as SVP and health and safety director. Cooter brings more than 20 years of safety leadership experience, most recently as VP of safety, health, and environment at AECOM. Strategic Storage Trust VI, Inc., a public non-traded REIT sponsored by an affiliate of SmartStop Self Storage REIT, Inc., completed its merger with Strategic Storage Growth Trust III, Inc., a private REIT also sponsored by a SmartStop affiliate. The all-stock transaction, which values SSGT III’s real estate portfolio at approximately $500 million, unites two SmartStop-sponsored REITs into a single, significantly larger company with more than $1 billion in total assets. In this capacity, he oversees daily operations while also reporting on both local/regional markets and national trends, covering individual transactions across all property types, as well as delving into broader subject matter. He produces 11-15 daily news stories per day and works with the Connect team and clients to develop longer-form content, ranging from Q&As to thought-leadership pieces. Prior to joining Connect, Paul was Managing Editor for both Real Estate Forum and GlobeSt.com at American Lawyer Media, where he oversaw operations at both publications while also producing daily news and feature-length articles. His tenure in B2B publishing stretches back into the print era, and he has served as Editor in Chief on four national trade publications. Since 1999, Paul has volunteered as the newsletter editor of passenger rail advocacy groups (one national, one local).
